ideas.title: Retention Pay Check for Childcare Centres on Xero Payroll AU

notes.stateful: Keeps each worker's award level and status, effective-dated retention rate tables, and a per-worker, per-period ledger of retention pay.
notes.connected: Reads draft pay runs, payslips, employees, pay items and timesheets through the Xero Payroll AU API with the centre's own login.
notes.unattended: A scheduled job checks each new draft pay run before it is posted and emails the person running pay when lines are missing, doubled or wrong.
notes.engine: Works out each eligible worker's expected Worker Retention Payment from the award level, not the actual rate, across ordinary hours, leave and leave loading, with juniors at the adult rate and staged award changes applied by date.

buildPlan.title: Connect and check one pay run
buildPlan.delivers: Sign in, connect the Xero demo company, read the latest draft pay run, set one worker's award level and see expected against actual retention pay on ordinary hours.
buildPlan.acceptance: Deployed; a missing retention line in the demo company is flagged.

buildPlan.title: Rate tables and worker set-up
buildPlan.delivers: Effective-dated retention rate tables for the eight award levels, junior at the adult rate, over-award and ineligible staff, CSV import of worker levels.
buildPlan.acceptance: Tests show the right rate for each period across an award step and the adult rate for a junior.

buildPlan.title: Full checks
buildPlan.delivers: Leave and leave loading, a configurable overtime rule, duplicate detection (template plus timesheet) and a wrong-rate tolerance.
buildPlan.acceptance: Ten test scenarios pass, including the 'allocated twice' case.

buildPlan.title: Unattended alerts
buildPlan.delivers: A scheduled poll for new draft pay runs, Xero token refresh and an email summary of issues.
buildPlan.acceptance: Exactly one email per new draft with issues, and none for a clean draft.

buildPlan.title: Ledger and reconciliation pack

buildPlan.acceptance: The pack's totals equal the posted payslip lines for a test quarter.

buildPlan.title: Polish
buildPlan.delivers: A plain README for a centre owner or bookkeeper, phone layout, an accessibility pass, a bookkeeper's switcher between centres and a walkthrough test.
buildPlan.acceptance: The walkthrough passes at phone width and axe reports no serious issues.

ideas.summary: For owners and bookkeepers of Australian long day care and OSHC services on Xero Payroll AU: a check of every draft pay run for the Worker Retention Payment, and a ledger to reconcile it against funding.

public.summary: Check every pay run for the childcare retention payment before you post it, and keep the record you need for funding reviews.
public.problem: Your educators' retention payment has to sit on its own pay line, apply to leave as well as hours, and change every time the award steps up. Your payroll software has no feature for it, so you set it up by hand and hope nothing is missed, doubled or out of date.
public.forWhom: Owners, directors and bookkeepers of long day care and outside-school-hours care services that run payroll in Xero.
benefits: Missing, doubled or wrong retention lines caught before pay day
Rates kept current through each award step
Leave and leave loading included automatically
A ready reconciliation for funding reviews
No need to move your payroll to a new system

ideas.problemStatement: The retention payment 'must be separate from the award rate and it applies to normal hours, any leave, any leave loading'; payroll software has no feature for it, so bookkeepers keep it in a spreadsheet 'every payroll', Xero users find 'the WRP is allocated twice', and since 1 March 2026 the amount for each of the eight award levels changes at every staged award increase.
ideas.description: The app connects to Xero Payroll AU and reads each draft pay run before it is posted. It works out each eligible worker's Worker Retention Payment from their award level (not their actual rate), covering ordinary hours, leave and leave loading, applying the adult rate to juniors and excluding head-office and administration staff, using effective-dated rate tables that follow each award step. It flags missing, doubled and wrong-rate lines and emails the person running pay. After posting it keeps a per-worker, per-period ledger and builds a reconciliation pack of retention pay against funding received for funding reviews.
ideas.targetCustomer: Owners, directors, office managers and outside bookkeepers of single-site and small-group long day care and outside-school-hours care services in Australia that run Xero Payroll AU and take the ECEC Worker Retention Payment; family day care and in-home care only where they employ their educators.
ideas.buyer: The centre owner or director, or their outside bookkeeper, by card.
ideas.whyNow: The Worker Retention Payment was extended to 30 June 2028, with family day care and in-home care added (The Sector, 2026-06-18). The Children's Services Award moved to eight levels on 1 March 2026 and the payment now absorbs staged award increases, so each level's amount changes at every step (Aussie Childcare Network, 2025-12-19; OIA impact analysis, 2026-03-16). Xero's request for retention pay items is still 'Gaining Support' and unbuilt.

scoreRationale.pain: Complaints from several distinct payroll users and a bookkeeper, but the newest is 2025-11-25 (https://community.myob.com/discussions/staffing_and_payroll/early-childhood-retention-grant/904785) and the 2026 items are news and one vendor's commentary (https://www.hcamag.com/au/specialisation/employment-law/childcare-pay-rise-is-settled-but-payroll-compliance-risk-isnt/587927).
scoreRationale.willingnessToPay: A paid plan does the task for centres that switch payroll (https://employmenthero.com/comparison-table-payroll/); no paid jobs found, and the government estimates compliance costs per service as small (https://oia.pmc.gov.au/published-impact-analyses-and-reports/early-childhood-education-and-care-worker-retention-payment).
scoreRationale.reachability: Self-serve search only; Xero App Store listing needs the Plus tier (https://developer.xero.com/pricing) and the owner's stated network does not reach childcare centres.
scoreRationale.competitiveGap: Nothing native in Xero (https://productideas.xero.com/forums/967118-payroll-expenses/suggestions/49497542-au-payroll-ecec-worker-retention-grant); centres willing to switch are served by Employment Hero and foundU (https://www.foundu.com.au/industries/childcare); the eight-level award makes the manual set-up easier.
scoreRationale.feasibility: The Xero Payroll AU API exposes pay runs, payslips and pay items (https://xeroapi.github.io/xero-python/v1/payroll-au/index.html); award level is not an API field, so workers are set up by hand, and rules change at each award step (https://aussiechildcarenetwork.com.au/news/childcare-news/worker-retention-payment-update-award-review-payments-processed-key-deadlines).
scoreRationale.complianceBurden: Employee pay data including juniors' dates of birth and grant evidence (https://community.myob.com/discussions/staffing_and_payroll/allowance-for-worker-retention-grant/896250/replies/897228); a wrong flag means an underpayment.

review.findings: Rescored 20 to 19 (complianceBurden 4 to 3) and re-scoped to long day care and OSHC services on Xero Payroll AU, MYOB later. No free or native pre-posting check or per-worker ledger exists for a centre staying on Xero: Xero's request is still 'Gaining Support' with no customer comment since 2025-09-16, MYOB's answer is a manual zero-rate category, no Department or peak-body calculator was found, and Xplor and Tanda show no retention feature; Employment Hero, foundU and OWNA cover it only if the centre switches payroll. The 2026 evidence is not independent buyer pain: the foundU blog and the HCAMag article quoting a foundU specialist are one vendor, and The Sector reports the extension without complaints. Since the 2025 complaints, the award moved to eight levels on 1 March 2026 and the payment absorbs staged increases, so the remaining pain is leave lines, duplicates, keeping amounts current and funding reconciliation. Distinct from the published Pay Rate Scheduler and Fair Work Date Watch, which put award-rate calculation out of scope.

ideas.summary: For directors of small UK community interest companies with no grants staff: a shortlist of funders that have actually funded CICs like theirs, plus a bid calendar with reminders.

public.summary: Find the funders that really fund community interest companies like yours, and never miss a bid deadline.
public.problem: You run a small CIC and every grant search turns up funders that only accept registered charities. You end up paying someone to build a shortlist and a deadline calendar, or you keep it in your head and miss windows.
public.forWhom: Directors and part-time fundraisers of small UK community interest companies.
benefits: A shortlist of funders that have already funded CICs, with real examples
Funders that give in your area shown first
One calendar of every bid deadline, with your own earlier target date
Reminders before each deadline
A simple record of every bid and its outcome

ideas.problemStatement: Small UK CICs need 'a prioritised shortlist of 15 to 20 realistic UK funders… with deadlines, typical award sizes and eligibility', must 'check each one funds community interest companies', and want 'a funder calendar so we can plan the next 12 months of bids'; directors pay freelancers for it because most funder searches assume a registered charity.
ideas.description: The director enters the CIC's legal form (limited by guarantee or by shares), local authority, themes, income and typical request. The app ranks 15 to 20 funders from openly licensed 360Giving records of grants already awarded, showing for each how many grants it made to CICs (with links to examples), its typical award size, its awards in the CIC's area and the months its awards cluster, labelled as a hint and never as a deadline. The user confirms each funder's real deadline from the funder's own page or marks it rolling; the app sets an internal deadline a month earlier, keeps a materials checklist, sends reminders and publishes a calendar feed. A light status tracker follows each bid from research to decision.
ideas.targetCustomer: Directors and part-time fundraising leads of small UK community interest companies, especially CICs limited by shares, that are not registered charities and have no grants staff.
ideas.buyer: The CIC's director, paying by card from the operating budget.
ideas.whyNow: IVAR's 2026 survey of 1,200 charities found 69% significantly affected by narrowing eligibility criteria and 61% seeing funders pause or close (Civil Society, 2026-05-21). Open awarded-grant data now holds about 1.57 million grants from 356 funders on GrantNav. Tools built on the Charity Commission register (Localgiving's matching) and charity-only free tiers (Grant Genie) leave CICs limited by shares outside.

Plus a 12-month bid calendar') with one hand-built sample shortlist for a London borough taken from GrantNav data, a waitlist, a '£29 pack' and a '£12 a month' price button that say 'launching soon', and one optional question for ad visitors only: 'what do you use now?'. review.findings: Rescored 21 to 19 (willingnessToPay 4 to 3, competitiveGap 2 to 1) and re-scoped from small charities and CICs to CICs only. All seven freelancer jobs are grant-writer hires and six show no award; in the UK only one names the shortlist and calendar as deliverables. Plinth's free Community plan offers grant tracking with deadline reminders and claimed eligibility checks; Idox's Open 4 Community council portals give CIC-eligible search with deadlines and alerts in 54 areas; Grantsights published funders' CIC shares from 360Giving data on 2026-10-17 and sells a full tracker and calendar in the US. The remaining gap is narrow: CICs, especially those limited by shares, fall outside Localgiving's Charity Commission based matching and Grant Genie's charity-only free tier. GrantNav's CIC organisation type is an unverified addition, so CICs must be found by name and company number. Not killed: no single free product is confirmed to do the whole job for a CIC, and no rejection rule applies.

ideas.description: The register crawls a public body's website and lists every PDF with its linking page, its best-evidence date against the compliance date, whether it is tagged, whether it has real fillable fields and whether it sits in a service flow. For each document it proposes a category with the archived-content or preexisting-document clause and the facts behind it, and a named staff member confirms or overrides it, so the record is the body's own decision. It then generates an accessible, labelled archive page and a draft memo to file for staff or counsel to sign, and runs a request log with a response clock for accessible copies. A weekly re-crawl flags archived files that changed and new PDFs, and keeps a fix queue with page counts for remediation quotes.

State guidance asks bodies to document their exception method, and host add-ons are selling page-priced conversion of every PDF, so bodies are choosing now what to pay for. DocAccess installs on any CMS and its pricing page already asks how many documents qualify as exempt, and since 2026-09-22 it is inside Diligent's agenda platforms. Free PDF inventories are now common (DocAccessible, CASO Comply, Ockem, CivicPlus) and Code for America's ASAP PDF runs exception checks but must be self-hosted; nobody sells a hosted per-document decision record with an archive page, memo and request log. The mandate is unchanged at 2028-04-26 for small bodies but unsettled (DOJ asked about more relief; disability groups sued over the extension). Legal-advice exposure is a burden, not a blocker. The vendor's '$70,000 or 42 weeks' figure was dropped as vendor copy. Not killed: no free product does the whole job and no rejection rule applies.

ideas.summary: For teams building coding-agent command-line tools with a screen-reader mode: CI tests that assert on what a screen reader would announce, so status-line noise and silent menus are caught before blind users report them.

public.summary: Test in every build what a screen reader will say when someone uses your command-line tool.
public.problem: Blind developers tell you your progress line makes their screen reader read out bare numbers, your menu selection is silent, and redrawn lines swallow what they type. Today you only find out from their bug reports, because you test by hand with one screen reader in one terminal.
public.forWhom: Teams that build coding agents and other interactive command-line tools.
benefits: A readable transcript of what a screen reader announces for each step
Builds that fail when a change makes your tool noisy or silent again
The same journey checked against a real screen reader when you need it
A history of changes, so a fix stays fixed

ideas.problemStatement: Blind developers report that coding-agent CLIs make NVDA speak bare progress counts ('with three or four of them I can barely hear anything else'), move menu selections silently and hide progress until a turn ends, while the teams adding screen-reader modes test 'by hand with NVDA in Windows Terminal' and leave other terminals untested.
ideas.description: Terminal Journeys runs a CLI or terminal interface in a pseudo-terminal through a scripted journey of key presses, waits and answers. It turns each screen update into the stream NVDA would announce in Windows Terminal (NVDA's default Automatic diffing), and tests assert on that transcript: the selected item is heard, a status counter is announced at most once, typed words are echoed. A free documented recipe runs the same journey under real NVDA or Orca on hosted runners and reports where emulation and real speech differ. A hosted dashboard keeps transcript history per repository and emails when a change adds new announcements.
ideas.targetCustomer: Engineering teams and maintainers shipping coding-agent command-line tools and terminal interfaces that have, or are adding, a screen-reader mode.
ideas.buyer: An engineering lead at a developer-tool company with a closed-source agent CLI; open-source maintainers use the free engine.
ideas.whyNow: Coding-agent CLIs shipped screen-reader modes in 2026 and blind users still filed terminal bugs from October to November 2026; GitHub search shows 35 issues and pull requests adding screen-reader modes to terminal interfaces since 2026-08-30, tested by hand. Real NVDA has now been run on GitHub-hosted Windows runners by other projects, which makes a calibrated emulator practical.
ideas.founderFit: He teaches courses that use agentic coding tools, whose terminal interfaces are where these problems arise, and he ships a web app alone in days; his Screen Reader Journeys project already runs real NVDA and Orca in workflows for web apps.

scoreRationale.reachability: Self-serve channels only: GitHub Marketplace publishes Actions without review and Show HN accepts tryable tools (https://news.ycombinator.com/showhn.html); the owner's stated network does not reach these buyers.
scoreRationale.competitiveGap: No free tool does the whole job, but real-NVDA checks on hosted runners are a free do-it-yourself pattern (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185921) and terminal snapshots are free (https://github.com/microsoft/tui-test); the emulator and hosted history are what is left.
scoreRationale.feasibility: NVDA's terminal speech is diff-based (https://download.nvaccess.org/documentation/userGuide.html), so emulation is plausible, but fidelity is unproven and calibration takes weeks.
scoreRationale.complianceBurden: A developer tool with no student, child or health data; GDPR basics and redaction of uploaded transcripts (https://github.com/microsoft/tui-test runs in the customer's own CI).

review.findings: Wildcard review: rescored 21 to 20 (competitiveGap 4 to 3) and re-scoped to teams building coding-agent CLIs and terminal interfaces with a screen-reader mode. No free tool does the whole job, so the wildcard kill does not apply: Guidepup, tui-test, Ink's screen-reader mode and framework snapshot testers each do part. But real-NVDA speech assertions on GitHub-hosted Windows runners are now a free do-it-yourself pattern (one merged pull request in a desktop app in November 2026, another project's speech-assertion rig in October 2026), so the product's edge is a fast emulated transcript plus hosted history, whose fidelity is unproven; NVDA's default is Automatic diffing and its Windows Terminal handling is changing. Eight distinct accounts filed the terminal items; two of the five recent complaints (a hotkey feature request and a suggestion closed the same day) are not things a transcript test would catch, and all evidence comes from coding-agent interfaces. The only spend on CLI accessibility found was research interviews paid by a large platform, not testing.

runNotes.caveats: First run of 2026-11-28 (Saturday, institutional back-office lens; focus sources A2, A13 in place of B5, which is on the avoid list, and C4). Four regular ideas ship, all provisional (Retention Pay Check 19, CIC Funder Shortlist 19, Multi-Lane Party Booking 15, Archive-or-Fix Register 16), and a provisional wildcard (Terminal Journeys, 20); none came near the gate of 22, and none has a complaint dated within 90 days except the wildcard and Multi-Lane. Twenty-two new candidates were generated (11 with a small-business buyer, 5 aimed at the owner's interests) plus the four watchlist entries of 2026-11-27, three of them re-researched; 3 failed a rejection rule. Eight were researched: three were ended in research (15-Day Records Request Clock, 12; Year-End Childcare Statements, 17, floor not met; Booking-Tap Counter, 18, a free native path in Wix and GA4), and five were reviewed: four regular reviews, all rescores (Retention 20 to 19, Funder 21 to 19, Archive 18 to 16, Multi-Lane 18 to 15), and one wildcard review (21 to 20). Three ideas had survived after three regular reviews, so the review target was met; Multi-Lane, which survived the fourth review, ships as the fourth provisional idea, within the cap of four. Multi-Lane Party Booking is the watchlist entry Lane and Bay Booking for Square Venues (first seen 2026-11-27), re-scoped to non-golf lane venues. Selection constraints: ideas 1 and 3 are Small Business Ops, idea 2 is Micro-SaaS with smallBusiness true, idea 4 is Civic & Public Sector and the wildcard a Developer Tool, so no category has more than two; ideas 1 to 4 are substantial Multi-week ideas with build plans. The constraint of at least one Weekend MVP cannot be met: every surviving idea needs a platform connection (Xero, Square, 360Giving or a site crawl) and a scheduled job, and the one candidate that could have been a Weekend MVP, Year-End Childcare Statements, failed the floor. Ordering: Multi-Lane (15, small business) is placed before Archive-or-Fix (16, public bodies) under the small-business preference for totals within 2 points. Access: the subagents' shared WebSearch budget for one turn ran out during research, so several researchers finished on fetches alone; education.gov.au answered 503 throughout, so Worker Retention Payment rate tables are unverified; HigherEdJobs (C4) served its 212-byte interstitial for the fourth Saturday running.
